items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Maria Schneider and Darcy Argue and people that have all studied with Bob

ctx.x: Nicely said. Was there something different you learned from each of your — like Brookmeyer and Bill Holman, and did you seek these people out for a specific reason?

I guess, without really thinking about it, but I sought out Bill Holman because of, you know at least with Brookmeyer and Holman — Rayburn Wright was such an incredible orchestrator and just knew how to get so many colors. Like I said, I came here only to study with him, to understand that. With Holman, with the early recordings — well not with the early recordings but the recordings when Bill wrote for the Kenton band, where it was very linear, and every once in a while you’d get a chord that was just like, oh…
what was it like working with so-and-so and how was this guy like, and so I’ve been very fortunate in my life to have those guys.
